Here's a description of the provided plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between temperature and accuracy for three different methods. The x-axis is labeled “Temperature” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.1 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (Pass@8)” and has a linear scale ranging from 62.5 to 80.0, with tick labels at intervals of 2.5. A red line with star-shaped markers represents “On-policy RL”, starting at approximately 73.5 at a temperature of 0.1 and ending at approximately 78.5 at a temperature of 1.0, with a peak of 80.0 at a temperature of 0.7. A purple line with diamond-shaped markers represents “LUFFY”, beginning at approximately 75.0 at a temperature of 0.1 and concluding at approximately 74.0 at a temperature of 1.0, with a decline to 71.0 at a temperature of 0.5 before rising to 76.0 at a temperature of 0.6. A blue line with triangle-shaped markers represents “SFT”, starting at approximately 71.0 at a temperature of 0.1 and ending at approximately 73.0 at a temperature of 1.0, with a peak of 76.0 at a temperature of 0.8. A yellow line with circle-shaped markers represents a fourth method, starting at approximately 65.0 at a temperature of 0.1 and ending at approximately 71.0 at a temperature of 1.0, with a peak of 73.0 at a temperature of 0.9.
